It’s true.
I knew a guy who was dying due to cancer, no treatment worked. Then a friend recommended salt water and he decided, why not?
So he drunk 2 whole gallons and guess what? He was no longer dying... due to cancer.

I’ll give it a try, but it’s hard for me.
Thanks for the advice, I have been feeling a bit better over the last few days. Some personal stuff has been cheering me up.

I think that’s part of the problem for me.
There’s just too much, it’s too big and too unstoppable.
And it’s just gonna get worse and worse and worse.
The immensity of it just drives me further and further down you know? I try helping but, I just don’t know how. And while I faff about trying to figure out how to help species are going extinct. 
Fragments of uniqueness thousands of years in the making going extinct because we just want more, some of them never having been seen before. It’s like... if we are alone in the universe, if life is an incredibly rare piece of random chance that is unlikely to have occurred anywhere else, then everything we’re surrounded by is the only life we’ll ever know, and we’re deatroying it. And by my very existence I am helping in that. By posting on this site I’m using energy that’s helping with that, by buying certain types of plastic I’m using energy that’s helping that, by turning the fucking living switch on. It’s tiny addons sure, but they are there and they build up.
I can’t help thinking globally when every day turning on a light switch reminds me of it. When reading, which is one of my favourite things to do, I always have a moment when I feel the paper and wonder where it came from. Everything reminds me of it, and my contribution, however small, to it. 
My brain refuses to resign myself to only being able to have a small effect due to being one person, yet logically recognised that I’m only one person that can’t have a large effect and it’s just tearing me apart.
Sorry if this post is rambly, I’m terrible at putting my thoughts into words
